messages.subject: server.R script behavior
parts:
Dear Group,

I have a Shiny application that generally works well.  I am modifying the way that it gets the data.  The data is stored in an Excel file.

Previously, I stored the Excel file data in a ~/data subdirectory and read it using the 'xlsx' package.  This worked well.

But the 'live' data is actually (in Excel) stored on a MS SharePoint site.  I have been ftp'ing the file to a Linux server for the shiny app to run.  I am trying to eliminate the ftp step by reading the data from the Excel file from the Linux server (running shiny-server) with the Excel file still on the MS SharePoint site.

I have R code that seems to get the job done (reaching from Linux and R Studio to MS SharePoint and Excel).  It works OK when I run it section-by-section within the server.R file using R Studio.  But when I run it as part of a shiny app this same code seems to get hung up.

I think that the issue may be related to the initial reading of the data file (Excel), since the ui.R selection menu is blank (when run using shiny-server or R Studio shiny).  When I run the server.R code section-by-section, R Studio seems to indicate that the data objects are read, processed, and appear as expected. 

I have attached my server.R, ui.R, and data file to this note.  (The 'start_here.R' file is only for running within R Studio.)


Here is the console info that appears when I try to run the app using shiny (via R Studio):

> library(shiny)
> runApp()

Is this enough information for someone to take a look to see where I went askew?

Thanks in advance for any clues or guidance.

Cliff

For the record, I had posted a related question on StackOverflow, but this was related to getting wget and curl to work (both on Linux command line, and via R).  I think that this earlier issue is sorted out now and this question below pertains to the next step (putting the code to work via shiny).

SO:  http://stackoverflow.com/questions/27820219/read-an-excel-file-stored-on-sharepoint-from-linux-server-running-r-studio

If this new question below is ill-formed, I'm open to suggestions on how to ask it more effectively.

Thanks.

Cliff
